surprises: T1's bound already clears p_breakeven at the FULL 70.98 bp baseline cost, not just at some hypothetically lower cost -- the shortfall is dominated by touch ORDER, not barrier reachability.
T2 initially included 6 'flagged_sidecar' events Phase 11's own prompt says are never pooled with the 50 primary events -- caught and corrected before T3 ran.
build_cache() requires a _bounds table that neither it nor Phase 11's own t5a_dev_timing.py actually creates -- a pre-existing gap in Phase 11's code, worked around here rather than left blocking.

go.Histogram/go.Violin embed ALL raw data points client-side when given a full-size array -- chart 02's first attempt was 107 MB (9.5e6 points) and failed GitHub's 100 MB push limit; fixed by pre-binning (chart 02) and subsampling with quartiles computed from the full n (chart 03).
T3's effective spread is roughly FLAT across deciles 1-9 and rises only at decile 10 -- not the monotonic 'lower participation, lower cost' shape the candidate's premise might suggest.

T5's exact curve reproduces T3's baseline p_clear_optimistic (0.3885) to the 4th decimal, and sits at or below T1's upper bound at every swept point -- both consistency checks the design called for passed cleanly.
The required threshold (~11.0 bp) is not close to any measured decile -- the shortfall is roughly 5x, not a near-miss.

A concurrent peer session checked out a different branch in this shared working directory while T5's ~4hr background query was running; no data was lost (everything committed was safe on origin, uncommitted T5 output survived as untracked files across the branch round-trip), but it was a genuine risk. Flagged to the peer and to Cooper; worktree isolation proposed as the fix.
